rows.summary: A long-lived client process appears on all four client panels once it has exported twice inside the 5 m window (about 2 minutes after its first call). A short-lived CLI or batch job exports one point per process under its own random instance, so it shows in the job dropdown but on no panel, and each run adds a new set of histogram series (13 buckets + inf + sum + count per method/peer/error).
rows.remaining: Choose between docs, panel and Collector fixes (options); separately, per-run series churn from CI/batch clients is unbounded cardinality over time.
rows.effort: XS (docs) / S (panel) / M (Collector pipeline + live check)
rows.probe: Observability stack (deploy/observability compose) + hello-agent or deploy-agent: run `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4318 a2a send <url> hi` 50 times; in Prometheus `count by (instance) (rpc_client_call_duration_seconds_count{job="a2a"})` -> 50 series with 1 sample each, client dashboard panels empty; then run a client that loops for 3 minutes -> panels populated. Re-run after the chosen fix. A stable OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES=service.instance.id=cli is NOT a fix to test blindly: each run restarts the counter at its own start, so a series reading 1,1,1 has rate 0 unless Prometheus ingests start times.
rows.options: (1) Docs: say under the client dashboard (not only GenAI) that one-shot processes never appear and to use Tempo traces for them; fix walkthrough.md's 'thin'. XS. (2) Add a client-dashboard panel that works for one-sample series, e.g. calls in range by short-lived processes: sum by (job, server_address) (last_over_time(rpc_client_call_duration_seconds_count[$__range]) and on (job, instance) count_over_time(rpc_client_call_duration_seconds_count[$__range]) == 1). S, no pipeline change, verify live. (3) Collector pipeline for client jobs: drop service.instance.id (transform), cumulativetodelta, then deltatocumulative to fold runs into one long-lived series per job; M, needs a live check and adds Collector state. Recommendation: (1) + (2) now; (3) only if batch clients are a stated target.

new_findings.where: examples/deploy-agent/src/main.rs:236-276 (no purge_expired anywhere in the example); crates/a2a-protocol-server/src/store/task_store/config.rs:264-265
new_findings.finding: deploy-agent never purges terminal tasks. With DATABASE_URL set, retention silently changes from the in-memory default (10,000 tasks, 1 h TTL) to forever: `tasks`, `task_events` and `idempotency_keys` grow without bound. The audit raised this under A2, which was closed for its readiness half only; the README's 'What this does not cover' and containers.md say nothing about retention.
new_findings.scenario: Two replicas on PostgreSQL serving steady traffic for months: tables and indexes grow until list() and the claim/fence queries slow and the disk fills; nothing in the example or its docs tells the operator to schedule `purge_expired`.

new_findings.finding: The startup guards added in 413ce9a disagree about which schema they look in: the table and index guards use `to_regclass('name')`, which resolves through the whole search_path, while the applied_seq check and the function guard use current_schema(). With search_path = 'a2a, public' and an unrelated public.tasks, `a2a.tasks` is never created, the ALTER, the task_events foreign key and the idx_tasks_* indexes all resolve to public.tasks, and the store either fails at start or attaches itself to the other application's table.
new_findings.scenario: An operator follows the natural 'own schema' recipe (`options=-c search_path=a2a,public`) in a database that already has a `tasks` table in public; the A2A store does not get its own table. Blocks recommending a dedicated schema for A14.

new_findings.finding: Every Secret recipe uses `sslmode=verify-full&sslrootcert=/path/ca.pem` and says 'mount it there', but the manifest has no volumes/volumeMounts and a read-only root filesystem, and shows no ConfigMap/Secret mount for the CA. With sqlx's tls-rustls-ring-webpki, omitting sslrootcert falls back to the bundled Mozilla roots, which do not contain RDS's or Cloud SQL's server CAs.
new_findings.scenario: A user on RDS creates the Secret as shown and applies the manifest: the pod exits at startup (file not found, or an unknown-issuer TLS error without sslrootcert) and the startup probe never passes; the fix (a volume plus mount) is not shown anywhere in the example.

new_findings.where: .github/workflows/*.yml (no job builds examples/deploy-agent/Dockerfile or lints deployment.yaml); docs/audits/2026-10-29/README.md L18 note
new_findings.finding: No CI job builds the deploy-agent image or validates the manifest (no docker build of this Dockerfile, no kubeconform/kube-linter/PSS check). L18 records that the Dockerfile's build stages (cargo-chef install, cook, build) have never been run live either.
new_findings.scenario: A workspace change that breaks `cargo chef prepare/cook -p deploy-agent` (a new member needing a file .dockerignore drops, a path dependency outside the copied tree, a toolchain bump past rust:1.94) or a manifest typo ships unnoticed; the first person to find it is a newcomer following the README.

new_findings.where: .github/dependabot.yml:20-50 (ecosystems: cargo x2, github-actions; no docker); examples/deploy-agent/Dockerfile:18,39
new_findings.finding: The Dockerfile pins rust:1.94-bookworm and debian:bookworm-slim by digest, and nothing refreshes those digests (no Dependabot docker ecosystem, pin-freshness.yml covers SDK pins only). The runtime layer gets no `apt-get upgrade`, so the shipped image carries whatever Debian packages (glibc, etc.) the pinned digest had.
new_findings.scenario: A glibc or other base-image CVE is fixed upstream; images built from main keep the vulnerable layer indefinitely, and a scanner in the user's registry flags every build.

new_findings.finding: Every A2A_BIND_ADDR example builds its card URL from the bind address (`http://{addr}`), the exact trap deploy-agent exists to prevent. genai-agent's own comment calls its server-only mode 'a real deployment' used 'as a deployment template'. With A2A_BIND_ADDR=0.0.0.0:8080 the card advertises http://0.0.0.0:8080; the ITK image sets exactly that (A2A_BIND_ADDR=0.0.0.0:9104).
new_findings.scenario: A user runs genai-agent in a container with A2A_BIND_ADDR=0.0.0.0:8080; a2a-cli or any SDK client discovers the card and dials 0.0.0.0:8080, which on Linux is its own loopback, and fails with a connect error naming no host (see A21).

new_findings.finding: The front-page description still says deploy-agent has 'a `0.0.0.0` bind'; since B-16 it binds `[::]` and falls back to 0.0.0.0.
new_findings.scenario: Doc drift only; an IPv6-only cluster reader concludes the example will not work there.
